### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in replacement))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in replacement))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in replacement))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in replacement))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2539ad9860a3e43323fcf35ac80ffee47c8dec3e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `597a3d66bf608760a926b179626ba73f1d44cf0b` — the merge of head `ef8a82372fe56fd9bfdbcab53c1cf22ca6e45219` into base `2539ad9860a3e43323fcf35ac80ffee47c8dec3e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 597a3d66bf608760a926b179626ba73f1d44cf0b && git checkout 597a3d66bf608760a926b179626ba73f1d44cf0b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2539ad9860a3e43323fcf35ac80ffee47c8dec3e ef8a82372fe56fd9bfdbcab53c1cf22ca6e45219 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2539ad9860a3e43323fcf35ac80ffee47c8dec3e && git merge --no-ff ef8a82372fe56fd9bfdbcab53c1cf22ca6e45219

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2539ad9860a3e43323fcf35ac80ffee47c8dec3e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2539ad9860a3e43323fcf35ac80ffee47c8dec3e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `208c32c83be614a42ead3c34f8c1007d1e73b2fb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/mapping.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.connector-pull-undeclared-input-key-refused.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull-undeclared-input-key.test.ts, .changeset/33894-connector-pull-undeclared-input-key.md, content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx, content/docs/references/data/mapping.mdx + packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-input-schema.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/connector-nodes.ts, packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-connector.ts, packages/connectors/connector-rest/src/rest-connector.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/README.md, packages/spec/docs/SYNC_ARCHITECTURE.md (read, not reviewed)

Read at 2026-11-15T21:12Z. First review of this head, taken on patrol as owed; claim: comment 6901351752. Independence: implemented in a zhuangjianguo lane (domain:server#5); neither dispatched nor implemented by os-tesla.

### ① Derived judgments

Read: the whole diff from merge base `159757ab` to the head (8 files, +302 −11), the card, the ruling 6896271476, and the cited code at the head.

- **Same check.** `connector-pull.ts` (`pullOnce`, step 6) now calls `judgeConnectorInput(inputSchema, input, { refuseUndeclaredKeys: true })`: the very function and option `builtin/connector-nodes.ts:162-166` uses. There is no second implementation, so nested keys, array items, a `null` value (refused), an `undefined` value (absent), exact-case key matching, and which schemas read as open (`additionalProperties` not false, `patternProperties`, composition keywords, `$ref`, no `properties`, no `inputSchema`) are identical at both doors by construction.
- **Only narrower by the undeclared keys.** The option only ADDS violations after the `required` / `type` walk (`connector-input-schema.ts:275-288`); every input whose keys are all declared is judged exactly as on the merge base. No declared key is newly refused.
- **Envelope.** `VALIDATION_ERROR`, status 400, `reason: 'input_schema_mismatch'`: the pull door's existing envelope for this judgment, unchanged. The node returns `code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR'` on a step failure; the violation sentence (`'query.stale' is not an input the action declares (declared in 'query': …)`) is the judge's and so the same text. Each door keeps its own remedy hint, as the shared module's header prescribes. The refusal names key paths and declared key names only, never a value.
- **Every door into the pull.** `registry.resolveConnectorAction` has two callers in the tree: the node and `connector-pull.ts:691`. Every pull (a job's scheduled `pull`, a manual trigger, a direct `IAutomationService.pullConnectorSource` call) goes through `pullConnectorSource` → `pullOnce`, one judge site. A run stores no input: each run and each `retryPolicy` retry re-reads the mapping and rebuilds the input, so there is no old-input resume path that skips the judge.
- **The door-added key.** The input judged is the one sent, watermark merged in. The second judgment (`{ query: { [param]: from } }` alone) only decides whether the refusal names the watermark; it cannot refuse on its own and cannot blame the watermark when it is declared (the third new pin holds that).
- **Upgrade.** A stored mapping with a stray key, or a watermark parameter its `openapi` operation does not declare, fails every run from the first run after the upgrade (the target already holds a value), `sys_sync_run` `failed`, nothing written. Declared in the changeset, the semantic entry, `jobs.mdx` and the generated reference, each with the remedy. First-party affected: 0, confirmed (`connectorSource` has no hit under `examples/`, `packages/apps/`, `skills/`).
- **Producer shapes in the pins are the real ones.** `buildInputSchema` (`openapi-connector.ts`) emits a section only when the operation declares a parameter in it, and `rest`'s `request` declares `query` with no `properties`: the test literals match.
- **Pins.** The flipped pin asserts `code` + `status` + `reason`, both keys, handler never called, nothing written. The new file has three refusal pins and three named CONTROLs (declared watermark sent; first pull not refused; `rest` open `query`). The author's three ablations each go red on the pins that claim them.
- **Spec face.** Describe text only; no shape change, so no JSON-schema or authorable-surface baseline moves. The old sentence exists in exactly two files on the merge base and both are updated. The new entry is a drop-in file (`registry.ts` is generated and git-ignored); entry 18 `connector-action-…` is untouched, as the ruling requires.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/spec`: correct. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves, and both move. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset; the title carries `!`; the changeset carries the **BREAKING** banner, exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`registered connector-pull-undeclared-input-key-refused`, matching the entry id), the FROM → TO pairs and the one-line fixes. `Skills-docs: none` holds.

CI on this head: 68 check-runs, all completed: 58 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, 0 running. The PASS below is not taken ahead of any running check.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No security finding. The change closes a pass-through (a key no action declares no longer reaches the provider) and opens none.
- No file outside the claim's surface is touched. The three prose places the author names as left stale are outside it and are graded in ④.
- Release-owned pages (`content/docs/releases/`, `CHANGELOG.md`) are not edited.
- For the sync-in owner (ADR-0153 D2): the PR body's note stands; paging parameters the door will add are judged by this rule.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the published rule real rather than taking a capability away: `inputSchema` is the contract `GET /api/v1/automation/connectors` shows, and the ruling says every dispatching door judges alike. The implementation is the smallest one that does it, with one shared judge.

No must-fix.

S1 (should-fix) — A NEW mapping whose `openapi` operation does not declare the watermark parameter passes its first pull and fails every later one. The PR declares this and is right that refusing the first pull is outside the ruling. But the door already holds everything needed to say so on that first run: when `watermark` is declared and `from` is undefined, judge `{ query: { [param]: … } }` for an undeclared key and log one `warn` naming the parameter and the OpenAPI fix. No new refusal, and the author learns on the green run instead of the first red one. In this PR or a follow-up card.

S2 (should-fix) — `connector-input-schema.ts` now misdescribes its own callers. Its header says the node is the door that opts in, and `ConnectorInputJudgeOptions.refuseUndeclaredKeys` says "Off by default: a door that sends only keys it adds itself leaves it off until its own authors are told", which is the pull door, which no longer leaves it off. The ruling also says future doors inherit the rule; with the option default-off a third door inherits nothing unless its author remembers. Follow-up: correct the two comments, and either flip the default or drop the option.

S3 (should-fix) — `packages/spec/docs/SYNC_ARCHITECTURE.md` "How a pull runs" still lists only a missing required parameter and a wrong type, and its watermark bullet does not say the parameter must be declared. `jobs.mdx` links to that section for the watermark in the very sentence this PR extends. Follow-up card, one sentence each.

S4 (should-fix) — The changeset says an operation that "names no query parameter at all" refuses the watermark. That holds only when the operation declares some other parameter or a body. An operation with no parameter and no body has no `inputSchema` at all (`buildInputSchema` returns `undefined`), so the watermark is sent, as the changeset's own last paragraph implies. `jobs.mdx` and the `input` describe ("must declare it") carry the same over-statement. Fix the clause before the changeset is released text: "…(or names none in `query` while declaring a parameter elsewhere or a body)…", and say that such an operation starts refusing the day it gains its first parameter.

N1 (nit) — When the only undeclared key is the watermark parameter, the refusal still says "remove it from connectorSource.input" before the watermark sentence corrects it. Skip the generic hint when every undeclared key is door-added, or lead with the watermark sentence.

N2 (nit) — No pin asserts the generic hint sentence ("remove it from connectorSource.input, or declare it in the action"); dropping it turns nothing red.

N3 (nit) — "then let the connector re-materialize" does not say how (republish the connector entry, or restart).

N4 (nit) — The rule for `watermark.param` is written under `input`'s describe only; an author filling `watermark` reads the `watermark` row, which does not mention it.

Card acceptance: met. The door opts in with its own hint; the pin is flipped to `code` + `status` and ablated; the declaration lines, `minor`, the ADR-0087 disposition, a new entry (entry 18 not widened) and its own breaking note are all present; the ruling's additions (door-added key named, OpenAPI fix, no fault edge, docs, the ADR-0153 note) are present.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `208c32c83be614a42ead3c34f8c1007d1e73b2fb`
Reviewer: review-a (areas S1 + S3) · read 2026-11-15T22:01Z · diff read against the merge's main parent `159757ab` (8 files, +302/−11, matches the PR files list)
Implemented-by: session_01QsR2jTEivi2wogPpeo3xd5 (area S3 dispatch) · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM
Ruling reviewed against: 6896271476

**Contract face:** this is a declared narrowing with `packages/spec/src` paths, so the review is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Its record is comment 6901440860 (review#2, PASS) at this same head, by a reviewer that neither dispatched nor implemented the change. This verdict is the ordinary ACCEPT read and does not repeat that record.

**The open point (dev report 6901990244): accepted as a stated deviation.** A new mapping whose `openapi` operation does not declare the watermark parameter passes its first pull and fails every later one. This is the ruling's route, judged by what is sent: on the first pull the target holds no value, so the pull sends no watermark and nothing undeclared reaches the provider.
- Refusing that first pull would refuse a key the request does not carry. That is a new rule beyond ruling 6896271476.
- The delay is declared where an upgrader and an author look: in the changeset ("a mapping whose first pull wrote rows fails from its second pull on"), in the semantic entry's `reason`, in `jobs.mdx` and in the generated `mapping.mdx` row. Each carries the OpenAPI remedy.
- A CONTROL pins the first-pull leg, and the refusal names the watermark parameter and its fix.

Two ways to close the gap later, neither owed here:
- The record's S1: one `warn` on the first run when the watermark parameter would be undeclared. It adds no new refusal, and the area can take it as a follow-up card.
- A check at publish time that `watermark.param` is declared by the action would be a new refusal at another door. That needs a ruling first.

**What holds (rest of the diff)**

- **One judge.** The pull door calls the node's own `judgeConnectorInput(…, { refuseUndeclaredKeys: true })`. The second, watermark-only judgment decides only whether the message names the watermark, and it can never refuse on its own.
- **The envelope is unchanged.** `VALIDATION_ERROR`, status 400, `input_schema_mismatch`. The new sentences name key paths and declared names, never a value.
- **Tests.** The flipped pin plus a new file with three refusal pins and three named CONTROLs (the declared watermark is sent, the first pull is not refused, `rest`'s open `query` is not refused). The ablations are accepted as reported.
- **Declaration.** The title carries `!`. The changeset has the BREAKING banner, one ADR-0087 marker matching the semantic entry id, and FROM → TO pairs. Both packages take `minor`. First-party mappings affected: 0.

**Owed after landing (the record's should-fixes; the head does not move for them)**

- S1: the first-run warn, above.
- S2: the comments in `connector-input-schema.ts` that still call the option default-off.
- S3: one sentence for `SYNC_ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- S4: the changeset's "names no query parameter at all" overstates the case for an operation with no parameters and no body, because that operation has no `inputSchema`. This is release text, so the fix must land before the next Version Packages run. Fix it here as a prose-only delta, or in a follow-up that lands first.

The area files the cards and names them in the PR's Acceptance notes.

**Gates:** at review time 58 success, 10 skipped, none red, so every check is green.

## Contract review — delta

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d16e1609fe4de198bd2eccd7cd63b7a05564def4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/mapping.zod.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull-undeclared-input-key.test.ts
Prior record: 6901440860

Read: `git diff 208c32c8 4adce2c4` (commits `e74cc24f`, `4adce2c4`; 5 files, +19 −7), and at the head `buildInputSchema` (`openapi-connector.ts:524-578`), `judgeConnectorInput` / `collectInputSchemaViolations` / `declaredKeysOf` (`connector-input-schema.ts`) and `pullOnce` step 6 (`connector-pull.ts`). Nothing was checked out, built or run.

The head `d16e1609` is a merge of main (parents `4adce2c4` and `b4eea885`, merge base `159757ab`). The main side changes 233 files and none of the PR's 8; none of them is `openapi-connector.ts`, `connector-input-schema.ts`, `connector-pull.ts` or `connector-nodes.ts`. The PR's 8 files are byte-identical between `4adce2c4` and the head.

### S4 status

Fixed in all four places.

- `.changeset/33894-connector-pull-undeclared-input-key.md`: the "(or names no query parameter at all)" clause is replaced by "(or names none in `query` while declaring a parameter elsewhere or a body)", followed by a sentence on the operation with no parameter and no body, and when it starts refusing.
- `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx`: "must declare it" is now conditioned on the operation declaring any parameter or a body, with the same exception and the same "until the day" sentence.
- `packages/spec/src/data/mapping.zod.ts` `connectorSource.input` describe: same condition and exception.
- `content/docs/references/data/mapping.mdx`: the `input` row carries the describe's new text word for word.

No copy of either old sentence is left in the tree at the head.

### Sentences checked

- "An operation with no parameter and no body has no `inputSchema`": true. With no parameter no section is emitted, with no `requestBody` no `body`, and `buildInputSchema` returns `undefined` when `properties` is empty.
- "so nothing is judged and the watermark is sent": true. `judgeConnectorInput(undefined, …)` returns `undefined` (`collectInputSchemaViolations` returns at once for a schema that is not a plain record), so `pullOnce` calls the handler with the watermark merged into `query`.
- "names none in `query` while declaring a parameter elsewhere or a body … refuses it": true for a declared `path` or `header` parameter or any `requestBody`. The top-level schema then lists `properties` without `query`, so `query` itself is the undeclared key. The existing pin with a header-only schema holds this.
- "it starts refusing the watermark the day the document gives it its first parameter or a body, unless the watermark parameter is declared with it": true for a parameter the generator emits; see N1 for the ones it does not.
- "A `rest` connector's `request` … reads as open": unchanged and still true.

### Findings

No must-fix. No should-fix.

N1 (nit) — "declares any parameter" is still slightly wider than the generator. A parameter `buildInputSchema` skips emits no section: an `in: cookie` parameter, an `Accept` / `Content-Type` / `Authorization` header, and the header or query parameter the connector's own auth or an `apiKey` scheme fills. An operation whose only parameters are of those kinds still has no `inputSchema`, and gaining one of them does not start the refusal. An unresolved `$ref` parameter goes the other way: it opens `query` (`additionalProperties: true`), so the watermark is sent undeclared. The over-statement only ever tells an author to declare a parameter they did not strictly need to, which is harmless, so it does not block. "declares any path, query or header parameter the action's `inputSchema` lists" would be exact.

N2 (nit) — The new CONTROL pins the door's half (no `inputSchema` ⇒ not judged, watermark sent). The producer's half (an operation with no parameter and no body yields no `inputSchema`) is asserted by nothing in this file; the pin's title states it as fact. A one-line assertion in the `connector-openapi` tests would tie the two together, if none exists there already.

### The CONTROL pin

It asserts the right thing. `harness({ inputSchema: undefined, input: {}, stored: STORED })` gives an action descriptor with no `inputSchema` (the harness has no `resolveConnectorActionInputSchema`, so the descriptor is what `findConnectorActionInputSchema` reads), a target that already holds a value, and so a pull that adds `query.since`. The pin expects one handler call with exactly `{ query: { since: '2026-01-02T00:00:00.000Z' } }`. It goes red if an absent schema were ever read as closed, and it is the counterpart of the header-only refusal pin beside it. The harness's parameter type is widened to `| undefined`; no other test's input changes.

### Describe change

Text only. The `input` field stays `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()).optional()`; no key, type, default or refinement moves. The only generated file that follows is `content/docs/references/data/mapping.mdx`, and it matches. No JSON-schema or authorable-surface baseline is in the delta, and the gates that would catch a stale one are green.

### Gates

68 check-runs on `d16e1609`, all completed: 58 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, 0 running.

The prior record's S1, S2, S3 and N1–N4 are outside this delta and stand as written there.
